title: SCIM patch transformations and idempotency guards for tenant suspension flow
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: When an IdP issues SCIM PATCHs to suspend or remove users/groups we have seen: racey PATCH application across workers, non-idempotent transforms (double-removes), missing audit context for retry attempts, and tenant-level rate limits causing cascading 429s and noisy retries. Goal: Implement deterministic SCIM PATCH transform rules and idempotency guards for suspension/deprovision flows, enrich audit events to include retry metadata, and add safe admin override paths that maintain RBAC v2 invariants.
acceptance_criteria: All SCIM PATCH operations that mutate 'active' or group membership are run through a canonical transform that normalizes: op order, unique member canonicalization, and attribute case-sensitivity before applying.

Every external PATCH from an IdP with an Idempotency-Key or generated operation fingerprint is applied once: duplicate retries do not produce additional state changes (idempotency guard stored for 24h scoped to external_id + tenant).

Suspension flow uses a 'suspended_until' TTL marker (ISO8601 string) instead of hard deletion when the provider indicates suspension; admin console exposes both 'Suspend' and 'Remove' actions with explicit audit prompts.

Audit logs include: original SCIM payload, transform fingerprint, operation_id, attempt_count, backoff_meta, and applied_state_diff. Audit log entries are queryable per-tenant and per-user for 90 days by default.

Retry orchestration respects per-tenant rate limits: requests are scheduled with exponential backoff + tenant jitter; 429s cause delayed retries rather than immediate enqueue, and repeated 429s move operations to a tenant-specific retry-bucket with operator alerting.
Automated reconciliation worker can repair missed patches deterministically using stored transform fingerprints and checkpointed offsets; it must not reapply idempotent ops.
Feature rollout: enable for 10% of non-enterprise tenants, run for 7 days with metrics pass/fail gating before expanding to Dedicated tenants; no regressions in latency P95 beyond 20% of baseline.
Unit + integration tests cover: duplicate-op replay, concurrent patch application, tombstone vs suspend transitions, admin override audit entries, and reconciliation no-op behaviour.
design_decisions: Use a canonicalizer service to deterministically sort and normalize incoming PATCH arrays before they reach the mutator. This reduces concurrency conflicts and simplifies idempotency checks.
Implement an idempotency store keyed by (tenant_id, external_id, op_fingerprint) with 24h TTL; store contains applied_state_diff, operation_id, and timestamp.
Adopt 'suspended_until' as the primary suspended marker. A separate 'quarantine' boolean indicates tenant-requested hold vs platform quarantine for suspect deletions.

RBAC v2 mapping: translate SCIM group-to-role mappings via a deterministic rule engine. If a transformation would violate RBAC constraints (e.g., removing the last admin), the op is rejected and an audit warning created.

Audit enrichment: write a structured audit event into our audit pipeline including headers, transform fingerprint, idempotency key, and retry metadata. Keep a human-readable summary for console display.

Retries: implement tenant-aware retry buckets with exponential backoff and capped jitter; after N attempts (configurable, default 6) move to 'manual remediation' queue and fire a PagerDuty policy for high-impact tenants.
implementation_notes: Canonicalizer tasks run as a pre-mutation step in the SCIM ingestion path (edge layer) to keep mutators simple. This will add ~2ms median overhead but prevent most races.
Operation fingerprint algorithm: SHA256 of normalized JSON (sorted keys, trimmed whitespace) + op_type + target_external_id. Store hex fingerprint as 'op_fingerprint'.
Idempotency store implementation: Redis with hash entries and a background compaction job; fallback to persistent store (Dynamo/Spanner) for long-term forensic retrieval.
Audit pipeline: emit both a raw audit blob (for forensic) and a summarized audit event (for console). Use the existing audit service contract: audit_v2.write(tenant, event_type, blob).

Admin override endpoint must require RBAC v2 'identity:admin_override' permission and produce a signed audit_note; the override creates a unique override_id that is stored alongside the idempotency entry so a subsequent IdP replay can be correlated.

Reconciliation worker should use the op_fingerprint to detect no-ops. It will read the SCIM change log, attempt to reconcile only missing or failed ops, and not touch records where idempotency entries exist.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): run canonicalizer + idempotency checks for QA tenants only. Validate unit/integration tests and end-to-end flows.
Phase 1 (canary): 10% of self-serve tenants for 7 days. Monitor metrics: scim.apply.success_rate, scim.apply.latency_p95, scim.retries.per_op, audit.ingest.latency.
Phase 2 (ramp): 50% of tenants including some mid-market customers that have low-risk IdPs. Run reconciliation daily to validate no missed ops.
Phase 3 (enterprise): after 14 days of stable metrics, enable for Dedicated and Private tenants. Provide a temporary 'compatibility mode' toggle for tenants with incompatible IdPs (opt-out).
Fallback: if high error rate or >5% increase in manual remediation queue, roll back canonicalizer at the edge and keep idempotency only in the mutator as a mitigant.
